purpose: Deterministic research/data taxonomy metadata for all enabled and FFG research-universe assets. No trading authority.

sector_definitions.description: Insufficient reviewed evidence for a deterministic narrative classification.
Protocols primarily focused on decentralized lending and borrowing.
Protocols primarily focused on yield markets, staking yield, or liquidity yield.
Tokenized real-world assets and protocols whose primary product is RWA exposure.
Infrastructure used to issue, service, price, or connect tokenized real-world assets.
Decentralized compute capacity used for AI or GPU-intensive workloads.
Decentralized intelligence, agent, model, or machine-learning networks.
Decentralized physical infrastructure networks.
Base-layer blockchain networks with their own settlement and consensus.
Networks scaling or extending settlement from another base layer.
Decentralized exchanges primarily identified with perpetual or leveraged markets.
Decentralized oracle and external-data delivery networks.
Cross-chain messaging, bridging, or general interoperability infrastructure.
Networks and protocols primarily used for payments or value transfer.
Blockchain gaming networks, games, and game-economy infrastructure.
Stablecoin issuance, synthetic-dollar, collateral, and supporting infrastructure.
Institutional-grade financial networks and regulated market infrastructure.
Infrastructure connecting ledgers, institutions, and settlement domains.
Issuance, distribution, trading, or lifecycle infrastructure for tokenized capital markets.
Protocols and products centered on tokenized government treasury exposure.
Decentralized cloud, hosting, and general-purpose compute infrastructure.
Protocols with a material Ethereum ecosystem dependency or role.
Protocols materially exposed to restaking markets or restaked security.
Assets whose primary narrative is meme or community culture.
Decentralized storage and data-availability networks.
Decentralized identity, naming, and credential infrastructure.
Indexing, knowledge graph, and general decentralized data infrastructure.
Spot, liquidity, and exchange protocols not primarily classified as perpetual DEXs.
Modular execution, settlement, or data-availability infrastructure.
